tables.heading_context: ## 1. The Two Orthogonal Axes That Organize the Discipline
## 2. What the Module Owns vs Defers — the Boundary Table
rows: Disease entities, catalogs, natural history, and entity-specific grading/staging systems
The test **catalog**, reference intervals/ranges, panel membership, analyte time-courses, imaging **physics**
**Bayesian belief updating** — pretest/posttest probability, likelihood ratios, thresholds, action
The *clinical* differential and its cognitive-bias framing (borrowed by reference in `10`)
Normal structure and physiology — the baseline a lesion departs from
Immune-cell biology and signaling (this module owns hypersensitivity *as a tissue lesion*, `04`)
Organism biology/taxonomy (this module owns *how a micro/molecular result is generated*, `08`)
Gene/pathway mechanism (this module owns the *lesion*, not the normal pathway)
The general analytical formalism — calibration, LOD/LOQ, method validation (`08` applies it to biological matrices)
Statute/precedent; forensic/legal cause- and manner-of-death determination — **out of scope**

tables.heading_context: ## 4. The Guide Map and Reading Order
rows: This map, the spine, the boundary table, the four-pillar contract
Reversible/irreversible injury; adaptations; necrosis vs apoptosis; accumulations
Acute/chronic inflammation as a program; mediators; granulomas; repair/fibrosis
Edema/congestion; hemostasis; Virchow's triad; thrombosis/embolism/infarction; shock
Hypersensitivity I–IV as tissue-injury; autoimmunity; rejection; immunodeficiency-as-lesion
Hallmarks; benign/malignant; anaplasia; invasion/metastasis; carcinogenesis; nomenclature principles
Inherited-disease pathology; malformation mechanisms; storage/inborn errors as lesions
Physical/chemical/toxic injury; deficiency/overload lesions; exposure pathology
How a laboratory result is generated and bounded (the three-way split's anchor)
Gross-to-glass technique as principle/constraint (no runnable SOPs)
Morphology-to-diagnosis reasoning and the report as an interface
The diagnostic service as a quality system
Why a single cell dies or adapts
Reversible and irreversible injury sit on a continuum; the "point of no return" is a mechanism, not a clock
Why tissue reddens, swells, or scars
Inflammation is a *program*, not a synonym for infection; repair can restore or scar
Why a clot, embolus, or shock forms
Hemostasis is protective; thrombosis is the same machinery in the wrong place/time
How the immune system injures its own tissue
Hypersensitivity here is a *tissue-injury mechanism*; immune-cell biology is `immunology/`
Why a growth is benign or malignant
Malignancy = capacity for destructive invasion + aggressive/metastatic spread, not size/speed; basement-membrane breach is the *epithelial* criterion (leukemias/lymphomas qualify without it)
How an inherited or metabolic defect becomes a lesion
The gene mechanism is `genomics/`; this module owns the tissue consequence
How the environment, nutrition, or toxins injure tissue
Dose, duration, and host factors shape the lesion; exposure is not destiny
How a laboratory number is manufactured and bounded
The result carries uncertainty and flags; the catalog is `medicine/10`, the decision is `clinical-medicine/03`
How a slide is made and where it loses information
Technique is principle/constraint, never a runnable procedure
How a pattern becomes a signed diagnosis and report
The report is an interface; belief update and action are downstream
How the diagnostic laboratory is governed as a system
`08` owns one result; `11` owns the cross-process program
What condition a person actually has, and what to do
This module produces the finding; it never diagnoses a person or recommends action
